_comment: Guided tour. Targets are view.json actions/attrs (their form rects) or window keys; 'await' steps wait for the outcome (data_loaded, analysed) the app reports, not for a button press. 'mode' and 'window' put the right mode and window in front.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text: This page checks a confocal smFRET measurement and finds its bursts. All processing happens in your browser: the file is analysed on this computer and no data ends up on any server. The tour takes about two minutes.

steps.title: Open data
steps.text: Drop a TTTR file (PTU, HT3, SPC, SM, PTO, ...) on the window. No file at hand? Open Try it without a file, choose an example and press Simulate.

await.hint: Drop a file, or press Simulate under Try it without a file.

steps.title: What was detected
steps.text: The page has read the photons: the excitation (cw, PIE or µsALEX), which detectors are donor and acceptor, and polarization. Lines starting with ! are guesses the data could not settle; check them.

steps.title: The verdict
steps.text: Quality rates the measurement. The basic checks need no ALEX: burst density, the share of bursts with more than one molecule, stability, background. Hover a check for what it means.

steps.title: Multi-molecule events
steps.text: The gap histogram (right) shows how bursts follow each other. Random arrivals give the orange curve. A big excess of short gaps means fragmented bursts or molecules coming back. If multi-molecule events is above about 5 %, dilute by the factor under dilution.

steps.title: E and S
steps.text: E / S shows the proximity ratio against the stoichiometry. With cw excitation only E is shown, because S needs alternating lasers.

steps.title: Advanced mode
steps.text: Switch Mode to Advanced to check and edit the channels, the burst search and the corrections.

steps.title: Channels and windows
steps.text: Channels shows the micro-time histogram of every detector, with the excitation windows marked. Fix a wrong guess here and press Apply.

steps.title: The time trace
steps.text: Time trace shows the count rate of each stream in 1 ms bins, with the bursts shaded. Use it to judge the burst search.

steps.title: Explore the bursts in ndX
steps.text: ndX holds the full burst table: lifetimes, anisotropies, TGX−TRR, 2CDE, the QC flags. Choose any two columns, gate populations and follow them through the other dimensions.

steps.title: Take it with you
steps.text: Bursts (.csv) downloads the burst table (ChiSurf names; ndX and ChiSurf open it). QC report (.json) downloads the verdict. Help explains every check and setting.
